title: Meta Ads Research: Arizona Full Report
summary: Full Arizona HVAC, plumbing, roofing, and construction Meta Ads Library research.
content:
Meta Ads Library Research: Arizona HVAC, Plumbing, Roofing & Construction Companies

Research Date: March 10, 2026 Researcher: Cleo (AOM Content Agent) Source: Meta Ad Library (facebook.com/ads/library) + company profiles + industry data

Executive Summary

We audited 30+ Arizona HVAC, plumbing, roofing, and general contracting companies through the Meta Ad Library to understand who is actively running Facebook/Instagram ads, what their ads look like, and where the quality gaps are.

The bottom line: The Arizona home services ad landscape is dominated by 2-3 big spenders running templated campaigns. The vast majority of mid-size contractors either run zero paid ads or rely on low-quality stock graphics. Professional video content is extremely rare. This is a massive opening for AOM.

Companies Currently Running Active Meta Ads

1. Goettl Air Conditioning & Plumbing

  • Type: HVAC, Plumbing, Water Treatment
  • Active Ads: ~780 results (highest volume of any company researched)
  • Ad Formats: Mix of static images and video. Heavy use of branded graphics with consistent orange/blue color scheme.
  • What They Promote:
    • "$299 Mini-Jet Drain Clear" (service-specific pricing)
    • "$50 off Early Bird Special, book by April 30" (seasonal urgency)
    • "Home Comfort for Less Than $100/Month" (insulation upsell)
    • "$149 Duct Cleaning" (entry-level offer)
    • "5-Star Furnace Service" with checklist format
    • "Kindness in the Air" (community/charity campaign with CBS Austin)
    • Water quality/reverse osmosis (fear-based: "Worried about what's in your water?")
    • "Breathe Cleaner Air" (indoor air quality)
  • Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads
  • Multiple versions per creative: 3-14 ads per creative (heavy A/B testing)
  • Estimated Spend Level: HIGH ($10k-50k+/month based on volume and multi-version testing)
  • Quality Assessment: PROFESSIONAL. Consistent branding, clean graphics, real photos of technicians. However, most creatives are static images with text overlays, not cinematic video. Their video content is functional (testimonial-style, product demos) but not visually impressive.
  • Website: goettl.com
  • Professional Video/Photo: Yes, but template-driven. Real technician photos mixed with stock lifestyle imagery. No cinematic production quality.
  • AOM Opportunity: Their volume is high but their creative ceiling is low. A competitor with truly cinematic content would stand out dramatically against Goettl's templated approach.

2. George Brazil Air Conditioning & Heating

  • Type: HVAC
  • Active Ads: 4 active ads (all launched March 2, 2026)
  • Ad Formats: 3 video ads, 1 static image
  • What They Promote:
    • "Oldest Furnace Contest" (engagement/contest format, static image)
    • "$1,500 Off Ductless Mini-Split Install" (video, "Get Offer" CTA)
    • "$59 HVAC System Check-Up" (video, "Get Offer" CTA)
    • "$4,000 Off Comfort Select HVAC Systems" (video, "Get Offer" CTA)
  • Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads
  • Estimated Spend Level: MODERATE ($2k-5k/month)
  • Quality Assessment: MID-TIER. The "Oldest Furnace Contest" graphic is creative and engaging. Video ads appear to be simple motion graphics over product imagery, not filmed content. Consistent branding with the George Brazil logo and color palette.
  • Website: georgebrazilhvac.com
  • Professional Video/Photo: Partial. Videos are motion-graphics based, not filmed testimonials or cinematic pieces. The contest creative shows design thinking. Overall, better than average but not production-quality.
  • AOM Opportunity: STRONG PROSPECT. 70+ years in business, clearly invests in marketing, but their video content is basic. A professional video campaign showcasing their legacy and team could transform their ad performance.

3. Chas Roberts Air Conditioning & Plumbing

  • Type: HVAC, Plumbing
  • Active Ads: 2 active ads
  • Ad Formats: 1 illustrated graphic, 1 product image with text overlay
  • What They Promote:
    • "Not Happy About Your HVAC Quote? Get a Free Second Opinion" (competitive positioning, cartoon illustration)
    • "Genuine Lifetime Warranty on Bradford White Water Heaters" (product-specific, "Buy Once. Heat FOREVER.")
  • Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads (Ad 1); Facebook, Instagram (Ad 2)
  • Estimated Spend Level: LOW ($500-2k/month, only 2 ads)
  • Quality Assessment: DIY/AGENCY-BASIC. The cartoon illustration looks like a template or clip art. The water heater ad is a basic product flyer. No video. No photography. The "Serving You Since '43" tagline is underutilized.
  • Website: chasroberts.com
  • Professional Video/Photo: No. Zero video content in ads. Graphics are low-effort.
  • AOM Opportunity: HIGH-VALUE PROSPECT. 80+ year brand with a "Serving Since '43" legacy story that's completely untold in their advertising. They clearly have budget (multi-service company) but are under-investing in creative. Video testimonials, technician profiles, and brand storytelling could 10x their ad performance.

4. Lyons Roofing

  • Type: Roofing
  • Active Ads: 2 active ads (from Lyons Roofing specifically)
  • Ad Formats: 1 static branded graphic, 1 carousel with reviews
  • What They Promote:
    • "Leaking Roof? And What to Do" (educational content with checklist: identify leaks, tarp it, call us)
    • "Storm just hit, is your roof still protecting your home?" (urgency/weather-trigger)
    • Carousel includes customer reviews and "Fully Licensed, Bonded and Insured" badge
  • Platforms: Facebook, Instagram (Ad 1); Facebook, Instagram, Audience Network, Messenger (Ad 2)
  • Running Since: May 2025 (Ad 1), March 2025 (Ad 2) -- long-running, likely performing well
  • Estimated Spend Level: LOW-MODERATE ($1k-3k/month)
  • Quality Assessment: DECENT. Branded graphics with Lyons logo, phone number, and website. Educational approach is smart. The carousel with Google reviews is a proven format. But no video, no real photography of jobs completed.
  • Website: lyonsroofing.com
  • Professional Video/Photo: No. All static graphics and review screenshots. No before/after photos of roofing jobs.
  • AOM Opportunity: GOOD PROSPECT. Lyons clearly understands marketing (educational content, review-based social proof) but is missing the visual proof. Drone footage of roof completions, time-lapse installs, and before/after video would be a game-changer for a roofing company.

5. Ambient Edge Heating, Air Conditioning & Refrigeration

  • Type: HVAC, Plumbing
  • Active Ads: 4 active ads (all launched March 2026)
  • Ad Formats: Video, static images, real job-site photos
  • What They Promote:
    • "Welcome All Quality Air to the Ambient Edge family" (acquisition announcement, animated video)
    • "Rooftops are our office" (real technician photo on a rooftop job)
    • Air filter education ("4 doesn't equal 1" -- don't stack smaller filters)
    • Service area expansion messaging
  • Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, Audience Network, Threads
  • Estimated Spend Level: LOW-MODERATE ($1k-3k/month)
  • Quality Assessment: BEST AUTHENTICITY. The rooftop photo with a real technician is the most authentic-feeling ad in the entire research. The educational filter tip shows expertise. The branded van/truck shot is strong. This company actually gets it.
  • Website: ambientedge.com (Kingman, AZ & Las Vegas, NV)
  • Professional Video/Photo: Partial. Real job-site photos (strong), animated video for announcements. Not cinematic but authentic.
  • AOM Opportunity: MODERATE. They already have a good instinct for authentic content. Could benefit from elevated production on their existing approach, but may be harder to sell because they're already doing "good enough."

6. Kooline Plumbing, Heating & Air LLC

  • Type: Plumbing, HVAC
  • Active Ads: 1 active ad (launched March 2, 2026)
  • Ad Formats: Static image with heavy text overlay
  • What They Promote:
    • "$59 AC Tune-Up" with "Arizona Heat is No Joke" headline
    • Services listed: leaky faucets, toilet installs, water heater repair, drain cleaning
    • QR code on ad (unusual for social)
  • Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, Audience Network, Threads
  • Estimated Spend Level: LOW ($500-1k/month)
  • Quality Assessment: DIY. Busy design, too much text, QR code on a Facebook ad (misguided), dark blue background with stock imagery. Classic "owner made this in Canva" feel.
  • Website: koolineplumbing.com
  • Professional Video/Photo: No. Zero video or professional photography.
  • AOM Opportunity: HIGH. This company is spending money on ads but wasting it on bad creative. The "Arizona Heat is No Joke" headline is actually clever -- the execution just needs professional production.

7. Semper Fi Heating & Cooling

  • Type: HVAC
  • Active Ads: 1+ active ads (found via broader search)
  • Ad Formats: Static image with promotional graphic
  • What They Promote:
    • "St. Patrick's Day Heating System Giveaway" ($15,000 value, give away a brand new heating system with full installation)
    • Military-themed branding (Semper Fi)
    • Phoenix area homeowner targeting
  • Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, Audience Network
  • Running Since: January 23, 2026 (has multiple versions)
  • Estimated Spend Level: MODERATE ($2k-5k/month, giveaway campaign suggests marketing investment)
  • Quality Assessment: MID-TIER. The giveaway concept is strong lead generation. Graphics are basic but the offer is compelling. Military brand identity is differentiated. No video content.
  • Website: semperficooling.com (estimated)
  • Professional Video/Photo: No. Static graphics only.
  • AOM Opportunity: STRONG. A military-veteran-owned HVAC company running giveaways is a perfect storytelling candidate. The founder story, the "Semper Fi" values, the team -- all of it begs for video production.

Industry Advertising Patterns

What Arizona Construction Companies Advertise

  1. Seasonal Promotions (most common)

    • AC tune-ups ($49-$79) timed for pre-summer
    • Furnace check-ups timed for fall
    • "Early Bird Specials" with deadline urgency

  2. Service-Specific Offers

    • $299 drain clearing
    • $1,500 off mini-split install
    • $4,000 off full HVAC system
    • Free second opinions

  3. Emergency/Fear-Based Messaging

    • "Furnace emergency? We move FAST."
    • "Arizona Heat is No Joke"
    • "Storm just hit, is your roof still protecting your home?"

  4. Trust/Social Proof

    • Google review screenshots
    • "Fully Licensed, Bonded and Insured"
    • "Serving AZ Since [year]"
    • BBB ratings

  5. Giveaways/Contests

    • "Win a FREE HVAC System" ($15,000 value)
    • "Oldest Furnace Contest"
    • Strong lead gen format

  6. Educational Content (rare but effective)

    • "Leaking Roof? What to Do" checklists
    • "Don't stack smaller air filters"
    • Water quality concerns

What They Almost Never Do

  • Cinematic brand videos -- Zero companies running professionally produced video ads
  • Founder/team storytelling -- Nobody is telling their company story
  • Behind-the-scenes content -- No job-site footage, no day-in-the-life
  • Before/after transformations -- Roofers and remodelers are missing this entirely
  • Vertical video / Reels format -- Almost everyone is still running square or landscape
  • Customer video testimonials -- All social proof is text-based (Google screenshots)

The Quality Gap

Tier 1: Professional (Template-Based)

Companies: Goettl

  • Consistent brand colors and logos
  • Real technician photos alongside stock imagery
  • Multiple ad versions (A/B testing)
  • Runs on all Meta platforms
  • Still relies heavily on static graphics with text overlays

Tier 2: Mid-Tier (Agency-Assisted)

Companies: George Brazil, Lyons Roofing, Ambient Edge, Semper Fi

  • Some brand consistency
  • Occasional video (motion graphics, not filmed)
  • Smart copy and positioning
  • Limited testing/variety

Tier 3: DIY/Basic

Companies: Chas Roberts, Kooline, most smaller operators

  • Canva-level graphics or clip art
  • No video content
  • Inconsistent or missing branding
  • Too much text on ads
  • Misguided formats (QR codes on social ads)

Tier 4: Absent

Companies: Howard Air, Day & Night, Donley, KY-KO, Penguin Air (currently), most plumbing-only companies

  • Zero paid social presence despite being established businesses
  • Relying entirely on organic, referral, and Google

The gap between Tier 1 and "Best in Class" is enormous. Even Goettl, the heaviest spender, is running what amounts to enhanced Canva graphics. Nobody in Arizona home services is running the kind of professional video content that would make a viewer stop scrolling.

What "Best in Class" Construction Company Advertising Looks Like

Based on national examples and what the Arizona market is missing:

  1. Cinematic Brand Video (30-60 seconds)

    • Opens with dramatic Arizona landscape shot (drone)
    • Real technicians in action, not stock photos
    • Founder voice-over telling the company story
    • Professional color grade, sound design, music
    • Ends with clear CTA
    • Runs as a Reel and in-feed video

  2. Job-Site Transformation Content

    • Before/during/after in 15-second format
    • Drone footage of roof completions
    • Time-lapse of AC unit installations
    • Real reactions from homeowners

  3. Technician Spotlight Series

    • 15-30 second clips of individual team members
    • "I've been doing this for 20 years because..."
    • Humanizes the brand, builds trust
    • Low-effort to film, high engagement

  4. Seasonal Campaign with Real Production

    • Not a Canva graphic saying "$59 Tune-Up"
    • A 15-second video of a family sweating in summer, cutting to a technician saving the day
    • Production value that signals: "this company is the real deal"

  5. Social Proof That Moves

    • Video testimonials from real customers at their homes
    • Not a screenshot of a Google review
    • Genuinely compelling, emotional, sharable

The AOM Opportunity

Market Reality

  • 274 HVAC contractors in Phoenix alone (per ByteScraper data)
  • 89 have Facebook pages, only 42 have Instagram presence
  • Fewer than 10 are running active Meta ads with any consistency
  • Of those 10, ZERO are running professional video content
  • The average Facebook click costs just $0.69 for HVAC -- meaning better creative = dramatically more leads per dollar

What AOM Can Offer These Companies

  1. Monthly Social Media Retainer ($3k/month target)

    • Professional video content (1-2 shoots per month)
    • 8-12 social posts per month (video, carousel, static)
    • Ad creative production for Meta campaigns
    • Strategy and posting schedule

  2. One-Time Brand Video Package ($5k-9k)

    • Cinematic brand story (60-90 seconds)
    • 4-6 shorter cuts for social ads
    • Drone footage
    • Technician/team spotlights

  3. Ad Creative Refresh Package ($2k-4k)

    • Audit current ads (most are bad)
    • Produce 10-15 ad creatives (video + static)
    • A/B test variations
    • Delivered ready to upload

The Pitch

"We looked at every HVAC, plumbing, and roofing company in Arizona running Facebook and Instagram ads. Here's what we found: the biggest spender in the state is running enhanced Canva graphics. Nobody -- not a single company -- is running professional video content. Your competitors are spending $5-50k/month on ads that look like they were made in 10 minutes. Imagine what would happen if your ads were the ones that made people stop scrolling."

Competitive Intelligence: Marketing Agencies Serving This Space

During the research, we also identified agencies actively advertising TO home service companies on Meta:

  • TAPLocal -- Running ads for Google Local Service Ads, targeting HVAC/plumbing companies. "Book More Jobs Today!"
  • Alpha Power Solutions -- Targeting roofers. "60-80 qualified inspections per month."
  • Bonsai Marketing LLC -- Targeting roofing businesses over $50k/month. "60 qualified roof appointments in 90 days."
  • VIZTEK Studios -- Phoenix-based. Created Penguin Air's award-winning campaign. Video production + brand overhaul.
  • Blue Corona -- Penguin Air case study. Digital marketing agency.
  • Big League Creative -- "We Build Legends." Worked with Penguin Air.
  • RS Gonzales -- Phoenix HVAC marketing specialist. SEO + social + ads.
  • RYNO Strategic Solutions -- Social media marketing for HVAC, electrical, plumbing, roofing.

Key takeaway: The lead-gen agencies (TAPLocal, Alpha Power, Bonsai) are selling appointment-setting services. The creative agencies (VIZTEK, Big League) have done good work but are not consistently visible. AOM occupies a unique position: creative production that directly feeds ad performance. Not just "more leads" but "better creative that generates better leads."

Data Sources & Methodology

  • Meta Ad Library (facebook.com/ads/library): Direct searches for 30+ company names, filtered for active ads in the United States. Screenshots captured via Playwright automation.
  • Company websites and social profiles: Cross-referenced to verify business details, years in operation, and service areas.
  • Industry reports: HVAC marketing budget data from ServiceTitan, Hook Agency, RS Gonzales, Blue Corona, and Revenue Boomers.
  • Social media audits: Instagram follower counts and posting activity for key companies.
  • Third-party data: ByteScraper contractor database, BBB profiles, Yelp listings.

Limitations:

  • Meta Ad Library keyword search returns all ads containing those words, not just the specific company. Some results required manual filtering.
  • Spend estimates are inferred from ad volume, version count, and platform distribution, not exact figures (Meta does not disclose spend for non-political ads).
  • This research covers active ads as of March 10, 2026. Companies may have seasonal ad cycles that were not captured.
